newsitem.title: FRANCE: Usinor first half profits dive.
newsitem.headline: Usinor first half profits dive.

text.p: Europe's largest steelmaker Usinor Sacilor, privatised last July, announced on Tuesday that first half net attributable profit plunged by 65 percent and warned that second half earnings would be weaker.
Net attributable profit fell to 833 million francs ($162.6 million) from 2.36 billion francs on turnover that fell to 37.39 billion francs from 41.63 billion.

"Taking into account the seasonal nature of Usinor Sacilor's business, the group currently expects the results for the second half to be weaker than the first but to remain clearly positive," the company said in a statement.
The industry has been hit in Europe by destocking in all industries and slack demand.
Company chairman Francis Mer forecast later at a news conference earnings should pick up in the first half of 1997.
"All the conditions are there so that the first half of 1997 will show an improvement from the mediocre (first half 1996) figure I just announced," he said.
"The horizon cleared up during the summer but we will only see an improvement in results in the first half of 1997."
But Mer cautioned 1997 would remain a difficult year for the steel sector. "We are at the end of a disagreeable period but we are not at the beginning of a very sharp upturn," he said.
"It's obvious the year 1997 in our core sector (steel) will be a year of transition, a difficult year -- but it will be less difficult than 1996," he said.
The steel maker warned last June it was unlikely to repeat its record 1995 earnings performance this year. Profits last year soared to 4.43 billion francs from 1.01 billion in 1994.
It said on Monday the 10 percent fall in turnover from a year ago was due mainly to lower volumes as the impact from prices had been limited.
Net debt at the first half stage totalled 8.35 billion francs compared to 11.04 billion at the end of 1995. ($ = 5.122 French Francs)
